title: Mimi and Pocket's Big Swap
markdown:
Some days the sunbeams are extra sparkly and the birds sing a secret song. That is how it started for Mimi the meerkat and Pocket the penguin.

Once, Mimi loved sunbeams. She popped up from her sandy burrow, wiggled her nose, and stretched her skinny legs so the warm golden light could tickle her fur. Whiskers twitching. Happiest start to a day. And Pocket? He adored cool ice. Every single day he waddled with a happy bounce onto his special sparkly ice patch, gliding and dipping and tapping, flippers making neat tracks. Pure penguin bliss.

Until a big hot heatwave blasted the whole zoo, as if a cooker had been switched on everywhere. Mimi’s sunny spot turned far too hot for a sun-loving meerkat. Pocket’s ice patch began to drip, drip, drip. Puddles grew. A melting mess.

“This is terrible,” peeped Mimi, fanning herself with a dry crispy leaf. Her bright eyes drooped.

“My feet are practically swimming,” squawked Pocket. Melted ice dripped from his sleek beak. He tried to hop. His flippers skidded. No help at all.

Because of that, Mimi’s whiskers twitched with a zany idea. “Pocket. We need to trade something for shade cloth. From the reptile house. They have heaps of it.”

Pocket’s round black eyes widened. “Trade? What do we have that they’d want?”

Mimi tapped a tiny sharp claw on her chin. “You have ice. Lots of it. And I have bravery and a fantastic nose for adventure.”

Pocket looked at his shrinking patch, slippery and warm, hardly special anymore. He puffed his chest. “Okay. I’ll trade my ice for some shade. Anything to stop this melting mess.”

Because of that, the Great Ice and Shade Caper began. The big round moon blinked awake. Mimi and Pocket tiptoed out. The zoo was wonderfully sleepy. Not a peep.

“We need to be super quick,” whispered Mimi, her nose twitching with excitement. Every new scent, every shadow, made her feel alive and ready.

“And super quiet,” added Pocket, trying his best to tiptoe, though it mostly looked like extra-careful waddling.

First they crept past Bartholomew the hippo’s big muddy pool. Bartholomew was snoring with a sound like a leaky tuba playing underwater. Whoooosh went a big gurgly bubble. Pocket couldn’t help but giggle, a little bubble of laughter escaping him, but Mimi quickly shushed him with a gentle paw.

Next they dashed — as fast as a penguin can dash — past the giraffe enclosure. The giraffes, with necks as long and bendy as bendy straws, were fast asleep, their heads tucked up high. They probably dreamt of tasty leaves.

“Where are we going, Mimi?” whispered Pocket, his waddle getting a little more urgent.

“To the reptile house,” Mimi hissed back, her eyes shining in the moonlight. “They’ve got the best shade cloth. It’s like a giant cool blanket, perfect for cooling down.”

Finally they reached the big dark door of the reptile house. It smelled earthy and warm. Mimi, being the brave leader, pushed it open with her nose. Creak. The sound seemed to echo in the stillness.

Inside, slithery shapes rustled. Mimi’s fur prickled. A giant gecko with eyes like shiny black marbles blinked from a rocky ledge. “Halt,” he said, dry and scratchy. “Who goes there? And why are you bothering my sleep?”

Pocket gulped and shrunk back. Mimi puffed her chest. “We are Mimi the meerkat and Pocket the penguin. And we’ve got ice for trade.” She pointed. Pocket bravely held up their last ice block, shimmering pathetically in the dim light.

The gecko sniffed. “Ice. Interesting. A strange gift. And what do you want for this chilly treasure?”

“Shade cloth,” they chirped together.

The gecko chuckled, a dry rattling sound that made Pocket jump. “Very well. One ice block for a piece of my finest, coolest, most wonderful shade cloth. Sure to keep you frosty.” He nudged a neatly folded piece of dark crinkly fabric toward them. It looked wonderfully cool.

Because of that, Mimi snatched the cloth and Pocket handed over the ice. A daring successful trade. As they turned to escape, the gecko flicked his long pink tongue with lightning speed. Zap. He almost caught Pocket’s tail.

“Whoa,” yelped Pocket, spinning on slippery feet, wiggling just in time.

“Gotcha,” grinned the gecko, marble eyes twinkling. He was only being playful.

Until finally they did not wait to play. They grabbed the shade cloth, nodded thanks, and dashed past snoozing hippos and sleeping giraffes, back to their own homes. They hung the cloth over Mimi’s burrow. Instant cool. Perfect patchy shade. Pocket tucked himself underneath and sighed. Mimi stretched nearby, shade so much better than scorching sun.

Ever since then they always had just the right amount of sun and shade.

“Today,” Mimi declared, grinning huge, “is going to be amazing.” And Pocket bounced out from under the cloth, ready for whatever came next.
